solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support struggles to protect outsiders in these isolated places

parts.note: to support someone is to back them

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: wars are violent struggles

indicators.note: outsiders are the people on the edge, so only the first and last letters of the following word are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Fighting groups shield strangers who have come to remote spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outsiders' looks like strangers in the scene; it only asks for the outside letters of 'these'.
explanation.definitionFit: Backwaters are quiet remote places away from the main currents of life and activity.

clue.text: Insect left, having eaten last bit of that plant

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of the word
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A bug, having nibbled the plant, has moved on.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE swallows T, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is an Asian climbing pepper plant whose leaves are chewed with areca nut.

clue.text: Republic in which rebel Jack keeps quiet always

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the rebel's name wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: Jack Cade led a revolt in England in 1450
P is piano, the musical term for quiet
ever means always

explanation.surface: A country where an insurgent always keeps his head down.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kent rebellion of 1450; his surname holds P and EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an island republic in the Atlantic off the coast of West Africa.

clue.text: Exposure of wrongdoing that may put an end to game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an insider revealing misconduct

definitions.text: that may put an end to game
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the referee's final signal on the pitch

explanation.walkthrough: The compound word is literal in the second sense: a referee blows a whistle to finish a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Informing on misconduct within an organisation is the figurative sense; the referee's signal ending play is the literal one.

clue.text: Hawk a line put up for purchase audibly

parts.note: a tier is a row or line

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the spoken sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: to offer for purchase is to sell

explanation.surface: Peddling a product line by shouting it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the verb to sell in the street; it is the bird, and 'put up for purchase' is the selling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiercel is a male falcon or hawk, used especially in falconry.

clue.text: Had rest of shop's computerised equipment coated in bright colour

indicators.note: something coated in paint is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: red is a bright colour
EPOS is electronic point of sale, a shop's till system

explanation.surface: The remainder of a store's computer kit was painted a vivid colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had rest of' reads as having the remainder; the definition is 'Had rest', linked by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposed is the past tense of repose, meaning lay at ease or rested.

clue.text: Fancy women's signs being ignored by this man!

parts.note: W is the abbreviation, the written sign, for women
a pronoun pointing at the man in question

explanation.surface: A man's passing fancy takes no notice of the signals women give him.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the usual shorthand for women; 'being ignored by' reads as W set next to HIM. The surface pretends a man is ignoring women's hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is a sudden capricious notion or desire, exactly what a whim is.

clue.text: Linger in southern resort before summer's ending

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town on England's south coast, beside Brighton

indicators.note: a word's ending is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Staying on at a seaside town until the end of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to linger or hang about near a place, as if suspended.

clue.text: One securing property has to transform great room good for nothing

indicators.note: to transform something is to change its shape, so these letters are rearranged
one thing for another means it stands in its place, so a letter is swapped

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A buyer of a house must convert a large room into something useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for nothing' swaps one O of 'great room' for G before the shuffle; it reads like a worthless room.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgager pledges property as security for a loan, so is one securing property, in both senses.

clue.text: Learner in firm observed board meeting with odd down-to-earth characters?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: Co is short for company
L is the learner-driver plate
seen means observed
a counter is a shop's board or bench

explanation.surface: A trainee watched a board meeting with some strange but practical people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd down-to-earth characters' are beings come down to earth, aliens; the question mark flags the pun on a sighting of UFO occupants.
explanation.definitionFit: A close encounter, in UFO jargon, is a face-to-face meeting with extraterrestrial beings who have landed.

clue.text: Team expected to be most successful may get a roasting

definitions.text: Team expected to be most successful
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ..., the favourite team
second meaning: a lean cut of beef usually cooked as a roasting joint

explanation.surface: The favourites may be heavily criticised if they slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: A roasting looks like a fierce telling-off for the team; it is really the oven. Topside is a British butcher's name for a cut from the top of the leg of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase splits as top side, the leading team, and as one word names a beef joint cooked by roasting.

clue.text: Fuss from friend getting mean maybe with time passing

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: something passing goes away, so the word for time is removed from the longer word

parts.note: the mean is one kind of average
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A stingy friend makes a fuss as the clock ticks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy, but it is the arithmetic mean; take AGE out of AVERAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is tiresome, prolonged fuss or bother over something unimportant.

clue.text: Endless lightness in clues regularly — rule-book not much read?

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: levity is lightness of manner

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of the phrase is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's frivolous clues prove a rarely consulted rule book.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful one: Leviticus is the book of Old Testament laws few people read through.
explanation.definitionFit: The third book of the Bible is largely a code of priestly laws, a scriptural book of rules seldom read.

clue.text: Quiet game: by leaving, show sign of indifference

parts.note: the call for silence

indicators.note: when something leaves it is no longer there, so those letters drop out of the game

parts.note: rugby is a ball game
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a silent game shows they could not care less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by leaving' means the letters BY come off the end of RUGBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising and dropping the shoulders is the gesture people make to signal indifference.

clue.text: Desire to go after power in act of political expulsion

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone in power is keen to throw out political opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go after' places the desire word after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is the abrupt removal of unwanted members from a party or government.

clue.text: Novelist as one with a divine vocation needing to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard is to be spoken aloud, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.words: as one with a divine vocation
parts.note: in the manner of a clergyman

explanation.surface: A writer feels a religious calling that demands a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright, author of The Good Companions.
explanation.definitionFit: J. B. Priestley wrote novels such as The Good Companions as well as plays like An Inspector Calls.

clue.text: Tot enters the French arena, running

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the masculine French word for the
to tot up is to add
a ring is an arena for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: A small child toddles into a French stadium, at a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler but is the verb to add up. Running here is what tights do when a thread breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights or stockings that are running are developing a ladder, a vertical line of broken stitches.

clue.text: Invoke evil upon terrible empire concealing wicked act

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of the following word are rearranged
wicked suggests something twisted out of true, so the next word's letters are rearranged too
to conceal is to hide inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rearranged
rearranged, with wicked as the second shuffle signal

explanation.surface: Cursing a dreadful empire that covers up its crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate shuffles: 'terrible' works on 'empire' and 'wicked' on 'act'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprecate is to utter a curse, calling down misfortune on someone.

clue.text: Unrealistic contract is sealed by one journalist

indicators.note: something sealed is closed in on both sides, so the outer pieces wrap around

parts.note: taken as written
a deal is a contract
Roman numeral one
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter signs an implausible contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealed by' means the outer pieces close round the middle ones, as a seal closes an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idealised is pictured as perfect, better than reality, so it is unrealistic.

clue.text: Maybe give someone a shiner, a sort of fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: punch someone in the eye, split into two words
second meaning: a red Pacific salmon

explanation.walkthrough: A shiner is a black eye; to sock is to punch. Shiner is also a name for small fish, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word is to punch someone's eye; whole, it names a Pacific salmon species.

clue.text: Ridiculed performance — director admitted getting upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down answer the word is turned upside down
something admitted is let inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
DIR is the short form of director

explanation.surface: A show was mocked, with the director taking it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the director's feelings; in a down answer it means turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Derided means mocked or scorned, the same as ridiculed.

clue.text: Held in little credit is impersonator making fun

indicators.note: something held in is enclosed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit
to ape is to mimic, so an ape is an imitator

explanation.surface: A mimic who is poorly regarded makes fun of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making fun' looks like mockery; 'fun' alone is the definition, a caper being a light-hearted escapade.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful leap or a light-hearted escapade, so it is a piece of fun.

clue.text: Sailors led by south wind

parts.note: compass abbreviation
a ship's crew are its sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen steered by a southerly breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like a breeze, but it is the verb, rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw something is to turn or twist it round, which is to wind it.

clue.text: Poison from chemical company no longer in service

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed within it

parts.note: the Royal Navy is one of the armed services
Imperial Chemical Industries, a British company that no longer exists

explanation.surface: A toxin made by a chemical firm that has been withdrawn from use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer in service' reads as retired, but 'no longer' describes ICI, the defunct British chemicals giant, and 'service' is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a highly toxic protein extracted from castor beans, a notorious poison.

clue.text: My turning up before fast, needing to shed weight?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the next word reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone shows up before a fast, overweight and needing to slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, not the possessive. The question mark marks a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpulent person is fat, so is someone who could do with losing a few pounds.

clue.text: Go over street location for meeting

parts.note: to have a go is to try
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Check a street as a place to meet up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over' looks like a phrase meaning check; 'over' simply puts TRY above ST in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a lovers' secret meeting, and also the place appointed for one.

clue.text: Contemptible folk at one time, heading off for freedom

indicators.note: with its head gone the word loses its first letter

parts.note: lice is an insult for despicable people
once means formerly

explanation.surface: Once-despised people set out for liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling contemptible people lice is an old insult; 'heading off' acts only on the word for 'at one time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence is freedom or permission to act as one likes.

clue.text: The same again — duck dished out with some herb

indicators.note: dished out means handed over and gone, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: ditto means the same as before
a duck is a score of nought in cricket
any can mean some

explanation.surface: The same dinner again: roast duck served with herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird served at table; it is the cricket zero, O, removed from DITTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dittany is an aromatic plant, used in herbal remedies and cookery, so it qualifies as a herb.

clue.text: No going back to King for countryman who rebelled against him?

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An American who once defied the British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is the King: the American colonists rebelled against George III.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yank is an American, a citizen of the country that revolted against the British Crown.

clue.text: Offer money, tons, to get newcomers

parts.note: to tender is to offer
a fee is money paid
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Pay out lots of cash to attract fresh recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offer money' looks like one phrase, but it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderfeet are inexperienced beginners, a term originally for new arrivals in the frontier West.
